kidnap_ab.definition: Fresh simulator per trial (full_world_robo traverse:=true + lab_stack with the mission parameters merged with nav2_loc_<arm>.yaml). real.label: measured: recorded drives replayed into each backend (1.0x requested, online) and coco_lab, identical scans and wheel odometry; scored by coco_lab.mapeval against the Phase 1B ground-truth raster
notes: Every backend run plays the drive at 1.0x requested; the player ran at ~0.68x (s1_tour, 649 s for 441 s) and ~0.76x (1_tour, 582 s for 440 s) of wall time, so the backends saw sim time slower than real time.

Rounds r1 and r2 ran slam_toolbox's ASYNC node (the project's slam.launch.py) with other sessions' simulators loading the machine (load averages 1.6 to 37); round 'sync' ran its SYNC node (same params, every scan processed) at loads 1.5 to 5: the results agree to 3 decimals, so load did not decide them.

Loop closure ON made slam_toolbox's map much worse on 1_tour (F1 0.40 vs 0.90, identical in all three rounds) and Cartographer's worse on both tours (F1 0.17-0.20 vs 0.88-0.92). Measured and reproduced; NOT attributed: the backends' pose graphs are not recorded.
coco_lab's own loop closures were checked against the truth: 13 of 13 true (loops.json).

claims.text: Every controller drives the SAME global path -- one file, its hash checked in every run -- on the same robot with the same speed, turn-rate and acceleration limits.
Every number in the comparison is recomputed from the recording at site build by coco_lab; a bundle whose numbers do not reproduce is refused.
The moving person is seen by the LiDAR but has no collision geometry: it cannot push the robot. A contact is measured, from ground truth, as a clearance of zero.
After every change and every move, D* Lite's plan costs exactly what Dijkstra finds from scratch on the new map.
A robot whose map only lacks obstacles (never invents them) reaches the goal whenever the world has a route, and never steps into a cell it could have known was blocked.

Same answer, not always less work. Over 200 seeded Sketch worlds D* Lite's total work was below A* from scratch in 191 (median 0.59 of A*'s), yet in 188 of 2204 single replans it did more; and on the real costmap change of Experiment C it touched 3,209 cells where A* from scratch touched 1,114.

controllers.how: Samples (v, w) pairs it can reach within one control step (819 per cycle with the mission's settings), rolls each forward 1.5 s, scores each with critics -- obstacle cost, distance to the path and the goal, alignment, oscillation -- and drives the best. A critic can reject a candidate outright.
controllers.name: DWB (Dynamic Window)
controllers.shows: every candidate it scored (Nav2's own /evaluation), rejected ones in red

controllers.how: Samples 2,000 noisy control sequences 2.8 s long, scores each whole trajectory with critics, and AVERAGES them, weighted by exp(-cost / temperature). The command is a blend of good trajectories, not the single best one.
controllers.name: MPPI (Model Predictive Path Integral)
controllers.shows: a fifth of its samples, as Nav2 publishes them (/trajectories) -- MPPI publishes no per-sample score

controllers.how: Chases a point 0.6 m ahead on the path along the arc through it, slows on tight curves, and checks that arc for collision -- and stops rather than swerve. It has no candidates: it follows the path or stops.
controllers.name: Regulated Pure Pursuit
controllers.shows: its lookahead point and the arc it checked (/lookahead_point, /lookahead_collision_arc)

challenge.score: Pass = the target found. Stopping early fails, whatever it saved.
challenge.task: Choose the order the robot looks in, predict whether yours beats the robot's policy on expected cost, then place the target and watch both search.
challenge.title: Find it

claims.text: A miss is evidence, not proof: with d = 0.9 a searched bay keeps a little belief, and the others rise.
If every bay cost the same to reach from anywhere, "most likely per metre first" would be optimal. COCO's bays do not, so the robot costs every order.
With a camera that can miss, nearest-first is beaten: a search that finds nothing drives the whole tour, so the tour's length counts.
Negative search: bay A, then B, then found in C -- each miss marked before the find. Giving up after A fails the challenge, whatever it saved.

The real mission is told the colour and nothing else: no bay, no pose. Moving the target, or corrupting the manifest, changes nothing the robot is given; the policy has no field that could hold the truth.
Silence is not a miss: a look with no camera reports is a failure, never evidence that the target is absent.
